question: The rock-cut caves of Ajanta and Ellora, famous for their murals and sculptures, are located in which present-day state of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ajanta and Ellora caves** are located in the **Aurangabad district** of the state of **Maharashtra**, India.
 
• **Ajanta Caves**: These caves are a group of **29 rock-cut Buddhist caves**, dating from the **2nd century BCE to about 480 CE**. They are famous for their **murals**, which depict stories from the life of Buddha and the Jataka tales. *Hence, the statement about murals is correct.*
 
• **Ellora Caves**: Located around **100 km away from Ajanta**, the Ellora caves consist of **34 rock-cut temples and monasteries**, dating from the **6th to 11th century CE**. These caves include **Buddhist, Hindu, and Jain monuments**. They are known for their intricate **sculptures**, notably the magnificent **Kailasa temple** (Cave 16), a monolithic structure dedicated to Lord Shiva.
 
• Both **Ajanta** and **Ellora caves** are recognized as **UNESCO World Heritage Sites** for their **historical**, **artistic**, and **cultural importance**.
 
• These caves are renowned for their architectural brilliance and artistic heritage, representing the **religious and cultural diversity of ancient India.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ajanta Caves:**

 
 
• The **Ajanta caves** are carved into a **horseshoe-shaped rock face** overlooking the **Waghur River**.
 
• They are famous for their **frescoes and paintings**, which use a technique of mixing natural pigments with a plaster base. The paintings depict scenes from the **Jataka tales**, which narrate the previous births and lives of Buddha.
 
• The caves were rediscovered in **1819** by a British officer named **John Smith**, during a tiger hunt.
 
 
 
• **Ellora Caves:**
 
 
• These caves represent **three major religions** of India: **Buddhism**, **Hinduism**, and **Jainism**.
 
• The **Kailasa temple**, one of the largest monolithic rock-cut structures in the world, was commissioned by the **Rashtrakuta king Krishna I** in the 8th century CE.
 
• The Buddhist caves include monasteries and prayer halls, while the Jain caves are known for their intricate carvings and attention to detail.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance:**
 
 
• Both Ajanta and Ellora caves reflect the **religious tolerance** and **artistic achievements** of ancient India.
 
• They showcase the **fusion of art, religion, and architecture**, serving as testimony to the skill and dedication of ancient Indian craftsmen.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Tourism:**

 
 
• The Ajanta and Ellora caves are popular **tourist destinations**, attracting visitors from all over the world.
 
• They are well-connected to major cities like **Aurangabad**, which serves as the nearest city for accommodation and transportation.
 
 
 
• **Preservation:**
 
 
• The caves are protected and maintained by the **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)** and are part of India's rich cultural heritage.
 
• Efforts are ongoing to preserve the **delicate paintings** and carvings from environmental and human-induced damage.
